# Best portable power station for camping

For most campers, the **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** is the best pick. The right size depends on what you're powering, so here are the options.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 250-300Wh)
This class covers phones, lights, a camera and a CPAP for several nights, and it's light enough to carry one-handed ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)).

- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249): 288Wh, 8.3 lb, simple to use. Jackery has replaced it with the 300 v2 on its own site, but the Plus is still sold through Amazon and other retailers.
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299): 286Wh with a 600W inverter, twice the Jackery's. It can expand to 572Wh.
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199): 288Wh with a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard AC-outlet version, not the "C300 DC."
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179): 268Wh and 600W, the cheapest real LiFePO4 option.

One caveat: OutdoorGearLab's lab testing scored the Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low overall. They rank as small, phone-and-laptop units rather than all-purpose stations ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)). Think of them as phone and light chargers, not fridge or appliance power.

## Multi-day trips or a 12V fridge or electric cooler (about 1,000Wh+)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It has 2,200W output, weighs 39 lb, and was recently under $900 ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)).
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's best value, on sale under $530. The fan is noisy.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799): about 1,070Wh and 23.8 lb, good for van or overland use ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)).
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**: WIRED's pick for camping. It's IP65-rated and survives drops, at about $1,079 ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Bluetti AC180**: 1,152Wh, 1,800W, about 35 lb, with a 5-year warranty. It's $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF according to the retailer's listing. Checkout has the final word on price. [Buy at BLUETTI via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (affiliate link, at no extra cost to you). It has no expansion port.

## Quick tips
- Turn off your CPAP humidifier. It can triple the power draw.
- A solar panel (Jackery SolarSaga or similar) extends trips. Non-Jackery panels on Jackery units need an adapter cable, about $25.
- These units are too big to fly with, since they exceed the 100Wh airline battery limit.

The review sites didn't give me direct purchase URLs for the other models. Searching the product name on Amazon or the brand's own store will find them, and prices change often with Black Friday sales coming.
